title: AI Agent Assurance
ogQuestion: Can you prove what your agents are permitted to do, and did?
intent: Commercial: assurance for agents that take actions through tools
brief: Agents act, so the assured outcome is bounded action: permitted tools, scoped credentials, approval gates, trajectory correctness and auditability. Covers tool use, agent permissions and human approval as one page rather than three thin ones.

title: Production RAG Assurance
ogQuestion: Is retrieval still returning what the answer depends on?
intent: Commercial: assurance for retrieval-augmented generation in production
brief: Retrieval and generation are assured separately. Covers retrieval precision and recall, groundedness, corpus freshness, embedding and index change, and permission-aware retrieval. Absorbs the retrieval and knowledge-freshness topics.

title: LLM Evaluation Assurance
ogQuestion: Does your evaluation still measure what production does?
intent: Commercial: keeping evaluation evidence valid after launch
brief: Evaluation is itself an asset that decays: golden sets age, judges drift, production traffic moves away from the test distribution. Covers regression evaluation on change, judge calibration, online sampling and evaluation coverage.

title: Model Change Assurance
ogQuestion: When the model changes, is the outcome re-proven?
intent: Commercial: re-proving AI outcomes on model version, provider or routing change
brief: Model retirement schedules, alias upgrades, provider migration and routing changes are production changes that arrive on the vendor's calendar. Covers version pinning, retirement tracking, re-evaluation gates and routing policy. Absorbs model routing.

title: AI Security Assurance
ogQuestion: Do the safety boundaries still hold against current attacks?
intent: Commercial: continuing proof that AI safety and security boundaries hold
brief: Prompt injection, data exfiltration through tools, and guardrail regression. Boundaries are re-tested as attack techniques and system context change. Defensive framing: what must be re-proven and what evidence is retained.

title: AI Governance Assurance
ogQuestion: Is governance evidenced by the system, or only by the policy?
intent: Commercial: operating evidence behind AI governance commitments
brief: Governance frameworks state obligations; assurance produces the operating evidence that they are met today: inventory currency, oversight that intervenes, monitoring, incident records. Accurate on regulatory timelines, no legal advice.

title: AI Observability Assurance
ogQuestion: Would you know if the answers got worse this week?
intent: Commercial: proving AI telemetry is complete enough to detect quality, safety and cost loss
brief: Traces and token counts are not quality signals on their own. Covers trace coverage, quality scoring on sampled traffic, tool error visibility and the gap between observing and assuring.

title: AI Cost Assurance
ogQuestion: Is each AI outcome still delivered within its agreed cost?
intent: Commercial: holding AI unit cost against an agreed threshold
brief: AI cost is a per-outcome threshold, not a monthly invoice. Covers cost per resolved task, caching effectiveness, context growth, agent loop cost, reserved capacity utilisation. Canonical page for AI FinOps; no separate ai-finops page.

title: MCP Security Assurance
ogQuestion: Do you know what every connected tool server can reach?
intent: Commercial: assurance for Model Context Protocol servers and tool connections
brief: MCP servers extend the trust boundary of every agent that connects to them. Covers server inventory, authorisation scope, tool description integrity, token handling and change detection on third-party servers.
